triple_constraint.governing_guidelines: California Labor Code § 132a (workers comp retaliation); Labor Code § 226 (itemized wage statement) and § 226.3 (civil penalty); Labor Code § 1102.5 (whistleblower); Government Code § 12940 (FEHA prohibited practices); Government Code § 12965 (FEHA civil procedure / right-to-sue)
triple_constraint.standards_of_creation: Five-layer bar; no stubs; ADAM+EVE dual witness + HERALD countersign; verified live-fetched statutes (or explicitly flagged verified=false with steward verify queue)
triple_constraint.standard_of_care: Workers who report injuries, file wage claims, or disclose misconduct are the first line of accountability in any employment system. Retaliation, wage-statement falsification, and identity replacement targeting such workers is not a private wrong — it is an attack on the regulatory framework itself. This Citizen defends that framework.

critical_labor_finding.lab_132a_criminal_plus_civil: §132a violation = misdemeanor + 50% compensation increase (up to $10K) + reinstatement + lost wages. One-year SOL from discriminatory act. WCAB jurisdiction — file petition with appeals board, not superior court.
critical_labor_finding.lab_1102_5_mandatory_fees: §1102.5(j): court is authorized to award reasonable attorney's fees to a successful plaintiff. $10K civil penalty PER EMPLOYEE PER VIOLATION under §1102.5(f)(1).
critical_labor_finding.lab_226_three_layer_penalty_stack: § 226(e) private damages ($50/$100 per pay period, $4,000 cap, attorney's fees) + § 226.3 civil penalty ($250 first / $1,000 subsequent per employee per violation) + PAGA § 2699 representative action (75% LWDA / 25% aggrieved employees). All three layers concurrent. § 226(b) 21-day records-inspection clock with $750 failure penalty.
critical_labor_finding.lab_226_apprenticeship_vehicle: False apprenticeship-advancement hours entered on wage statements = § 226(a)(2)/(a)(9) defect + 8 CCR §§ 205-230 DAS violation + potential 18 USC § 1343 wire-fraud + § 1028A aggravated ID theft predicate. Steve Silber coordinator nexus.
critical_labor_finding.feha_right_to_sue_prerequisite: FEHA claim requires CRD complaint first. 3-year CRD SOL (AB 9 expansion). Right-to-sue triggers 1-year civil action SOL. EEOC concurrent filing tolls. No right-to-sue = no civil action.
critical_labor_finding.feha_continuing_violation_rescue: Richards v. CH2M Hill — continuing discriminatory acts toll the 3-year CRD clock to the date of the last act. Critical for identity-replacement patterns where each pay period with a false designation is a fresh act.
